title: Manchester Encoder
constraints: Each data bit takes 2 clock cycles (two half-bits). IEEE 802.3 convention: a **1** is sent as low-then-high (0, 1), a **0** as high-then-low (1, 0). Bits go MSB first.

On an edge with `load` while not busy: capture `data`, set `busy`, and drive the first half-bit of bit 7 immediately (registered `tx`). Each following edge drives the next half-bit. The edge after the 16th half-bit returns to idle: `busy = 0`, `tx = 0`.
`load` while busy is ignored. Synchronous reset → idle.
hints: A 4-bit half-bit counter k: `tx = (k[0] == 0) ? ~bit : bit`, with `bit = shreg[7 - k/2]`.
Manchester coding guarantees a transition in every bit period, so the receiver can recover the clock, and the signal has no DC component.

examples.title: busy
examples.input: a second load during a transfer
